policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): The scene at this decision step is the LAST listed observed step; check that frame first, before any earlier execution frame. If any object line in that last frame ends in 'is held in the gripper', or the fingers there are partly closed (about 46% or less open), choose B: put it into the bin, before any other rule is considered. This holds whatever `placed` contains and however many cubes lie on the table. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Color choice: if the last entry of `placed` is a color whose required count is not yet met, pick that color again (one color is finished before the other is started); otherwise, including when `placed` is empty, pick any color that still has fewer entries than required. Point at that cube's center as shown in the scene at this decision step. A candidate is a cube of the needed color reported as a table cube (not held) at the same coordinates, within about 2 px, in every execution frame of this decision step including the first one (at step #1, with no execution frames, any cube of that color in the scene is a candidate). A detection that first appears during the step, that sits where the held cube was last reported, that is reported within about 25 px of the bin's center, or whose position moves between frames is not a candidate while any stable one exists. Among several stable candidates, prefer the one nearest the bin's reported center without overlapping it. The point is that candidate's center as reported in the last frame. Cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the stable cube of a needed color nearest the bin (not overlapping it), and if none is visible at all, choose A pointing at any visible cube not overlapping the bin. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

fields.name: placed
fields.description: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. When the carried-in memory is empty, write the literal [] as this step's value. The value is always a JSON array of double-quoted strings, exactly like the carried-in value and the example: ["green", "green"], never ['green', 'green'] and never a blank. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. The oracle always runs the put-into-bin subgoal to completion, so this held-then-released pattern is always a successful placement: append whatever the gripper position at release (it is often 30-50 px from the bin's reported center) and whatever cubes appear, move or vanish on the table in the same frames. e.g. carried-in ["red"] becomes ["red", "red"]. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. e.g. ["green", "green"]
